messages.subject: Re: Hierarchical mirt model
parts:
Hi Rico,

I have not added support for the higher-order model unfortunately, mostly because I don't find it all that useful due to identification problems (and because it tends to fit worse than the bifactor model). So, I just haven't been inspired to add this model to the package, but that's not to say it couldn't be included sometime in the future. Regarding your second question, some type of stochastic algorithm is probably a good idea for fitting an 8 factor model, such as the MHRM or one of the stochastic EM approaches. HTH.
 
Phil


On Wed, Aug 15, 2018 at 5:51 AM <rico...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi Phil.

I am analyzing SF-36/RAND-36 which is a 36-item quality of life measure, typically modeled as 8 first-order factors and 2 second-order factors. I read in some other thread that you were considering adding the option of higher-order models to mirt back in 2014. (1) Has this been done or is there a way for me to do so manually? It would be very interesting to compare the hierarchical model with the bifactor model (both for the total 8-factor model and two individual 4-factor models). I am also interested in the correlated-traits model. (2) Is there an algorithm you recommend for an 8-factor correlated-traits model or is the dimensionality too high?

Best,
Rico
